doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Hearing himself on TV and records; Hank Jones
summary: TV ads, not listening to his records, leaving rough edges, and Hank Jones albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And do you hear yourself on T.V. occasionally?

Yes I do. There’s an American Express one that I did that’s played a lot, and Applebee’s, which is a chain, I’m on those. That’s kind of a fun thing. It’s fun to hear myself on the radio once in a while too, on a jazz station. And actually I really honestly, I’m not trying to be falsely modest or anything, but I just don’t listen to my own records. It’s like watching home movies for me. It’s like it’s done, time to move on to the next thing, and I hear every mistake and everything I’d want to fix. And when I do my records, I purposely try to not do too much editing or dubbing or anything like that. I really like to leave all the rough edges in there. I think it’s real important to have a good feeling over everything being clean and antiseptic. But consequently I hear all the rough edges. But when you put a few years behind it, and all of a sudden you hear something on the radio, you say hey that’s really not so bad, that’s pretty good. In fact there was one record I did for Hank Jones where I’m playing alto, and I was out in California staying at a friend’s house and he plays this record for me, and I didn’t even recognize myself. Because I don’t play alto that much. And I said hey that guy sounds good, who is that?
That’s the one he did for me, but I did one for him called “Lazy Afternoon.”
What a nice gentleman he is.
Oh, great guy, and a genius at the piano, really. A giant. A complete piano player, really.
